title: Affine denominator maps are injective on a full-support module without embedded primes
statement: Let A be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and M a finite A-module [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] whose support is Spec(A) and whose associated primes are all minimal primes of A. Let a and b be non-zero-divisors of A, let q be the total quotient ring of A, and put I = {x in A | x(a/b) belongs to A inside q}. Then I is an ideal of A (and hence is finitely generated), multiplication gives an injective A-linear map I M \to M, and the rule x m \mapsto (a/b)(x m), interpreted in the localization M_b and using that b is a non-zero-divisor on M, gives an injective A-linear map I M \to M. The cokernel of the first map is annihilated by I, and the cokernel of the second map is annihilated by the submodule (a/b)I of A.
